item.description: Barrister say law does not adequately recognise power imbalance between young people and much older adults Allegations against Russell Brand and, separately, David Walliams, which he denies, have led to calls for greater legal protection for 16- and 17-year-olds from sexual exploitation by older adults. A staggered consent law is one route favoured by campaigners, supported by some Labour MPs. Claire Waxman, the victims’ commissioner for England and Wales, has called for “serious conversations” on the potential for legislative change. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: New genetic atlas reveals traces of 10,000 years of sheep breeding
item.description: For around 10,000 years, humans have selectively bred sheep for desirable traits. Generation after generation, we have chosen animals for their wool, size and reproductive characteristics and gradually left our mark on their DNA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient rocks reveal a dramatic journey from deep inside Earth
item.description: Surface rocks can reveal records of regions they occupied millions of years ago, even if those areas were kilometers below ground. On Türkiye's Marmara Sea's southern shores and islands, granitic rocks that are now exposed originated as molten material deep in Earth's crust. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Evolution found another way to build a primate brain
item.description: What makes the human brain so much larger and more complex than the brains of many other mammals? Scientists have long sought clues in our DNA. Some discoveries show how genetic changes enable the developing brain to produce more cells. Others help explain how long those cells can continue to multiply. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mountain growth spurts may have sparked complex life on Earth
item.description: Mountain ranges grew higher throughout Earth's history in two distinct "spurts" that correlated with the flourishing of biological diversity on our planet, according to new research published in the journal Science Advances. The study suggests mountains may have played a key role in sparking complex life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A likely supermassive neutron star might shed light on the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes
item.description: A team of astronomers recently identified a red giant star with an unseen binary companion after examining data from the Large Sky Area MultiObject Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). Although the companion object can't be observed visually, astronomers can see the gravitational effects it has on the red giant star. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ocean absorbs more fossil fuel carbon while land uptake stalls, 30 years of data show
item.description: The ocean has been absorbing carbon dioxide from fossil fuel emissions at an increasing rate since 1990, while the net uptake of carbon by forests, soils and other land ecosystems has not grown, according to a new study led by scientists at UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Water-activated polymer forms solid shapes underwater and bonds glass fragments
item.description: Cement hardens when mixed with water, allowing it to form solid structures even in wet environments. This property is known as hydraulicity. Reproducing this property in organic polymers has been challenging, as polymer materials that react with moisture often lack the combination of bulk curing and water resistance needed to harden reliably in wet conditions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Who lives in a sponge under the sea? Tiny Caribbean fish and their microscopic neighbors
item.description: Two new studies involving Newcastle University marine scientist Dr. Theresa Rueger have highlighted how the tusked goby's relationship with its host sponge shapes almost every aspect of its life. Rueger, a senior lecturer in tropical marine sciences at Newcastle University's School of Natural and Environmental Sciences, is senior author of one study and co-author of the other, which together uncover the influence of sponges on the tiny Caribbean reef fish's social behavior, growth, reproduction and microbiome. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: From stimulation to suppression: How nitrogen addition changes soil respiration over time
item.description: Soil respiration (Rs), the efflux of CO₂ from soils to the atmosphere driven by root and microbial activity, is one of the largest terrestrial carbon fluxes and a primary determinant of net carbon sequestration. The important role of nitrogen in driving terrestrial carbon sequestration has long been recognized. However, the role of nitrogen in the temporal dynamics of Rs has not been well understood. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Show HN: Isometric SF – A pixel-art map of the SF Bay Area
item.description: Technical Write-up: https://www.justinchavez.com/blog/isometric-sf-how/ Hi HN! Showcasing this fun project. It's really fun to explore and stumble upon various famous landmarks like Apple Park, Palace of Fine Arts, or UC Berkeley. The technicals involve using Nano Banana 2 to train a Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 LoRA which is used to prototype the style and generation methods. For final map I used Qwen to train a Klein 4B LoRA which reproduced the style at 1/4 of the cost… Fuente: Hacker News - Portada.

item.title: Self-learning AI separates particle jets from background noise in simulated heavy-ion collisions
item.description: A team of physicists and computer scientists led by researchers at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Brookhaven National Laboratory developed a new artificial intelligence (AI) approach that learns on its own to separate important high-energy particle jet signals from the enormous background of particles recorded in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, where two beams of heavy ions collide at near the speed of light. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Colorful fish reveal how species stay distinct despite interbreeding
item.description: Vividly colored fish dwelling at the bottom of shallow Midwestern streams may help biologists understand the evolutionary mechanisms by which species remain distinct despite their similarities and overlapping ranges. Orangethroat and rainbow darters regularly interbreed where their ranges overlap, yet—millions of years after they first diverged—they remain separate species. Fuente: Phys.org.

La premisa detrás de esta tecnología es sencilla: en lugar de aplicar programas rígidos iguales para todo el mundo, la máquina va calibrando su funcionamiento en función de cómo ha quedado la colada… Fuente: Xataka.
